title: Commitment Reconciliation: Align top-account promises to cycle capacity & escalation SLOs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a formalized process and lightweight tooling to reconcile committed deliverables for top accounts with the actual cycle capacity and escalation SLOs. Over the last two quarters we recognized several overcommit scenarios where top-account promises pushed scope past engineering capacity, causing SLA misses and emergency re-scopes. This ticket defines the initiative, acceptance criteria, and rollout for a "Commitment Reconciliation" flow that sits between intake (customer asks) and roadmap slotting (cycle planning).

Background & problem statement:
- Sales/Customer Success and PMs sometimes surface high-priority asks for top accounts late in the cycle; engineering capacity is already committed.
- There is no single ledger that maps account commitments to committed sprint/cycle capacity and expected deliverables.
- Lack of an automated risk signal means teams react ad-hoc (fire drills, partial deliveries, scope creep).

Goals:
1) Provide a reproducible way to validate whether a new top-account commitment can fit within the upcoming cycle without jeopardizing SLOs or existing OKR commitments.
2) Surface an automated risk score and suggested mitigations (defer, scope-down, add dedicated runway).
3) Feed reconciliation into the cycle planning ritual and console so engineering, PM, and Sales have the same view.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Reduce number of mid-cycle emergency re-scopes for top-account asks by 50%.
- 95% of new top-account commitments receive a reconciliation result within 48 hours.
- Fewer than 3 SLA-impacting escalations traced to roadmap overcommit per quarter.

Acceptance criteria:
- A lightweight PRD describing the ledger schema and reconciliation rules is published in Confluence (linked).
- An internal dashboard widget (Console -> Roadmap) showing per-account committed effort vs available capacity for next two cycles.
- Automated risk score calculation implemented as a job (inputs: requested scope points, cycle capacity, dependencies, current burn rate).
- Decision flow documented and integrated into the VIP intake form (Sales/CS flow) with mandatory reconciliation step.

Proposed approach / implementation plan:
1) Define ledger schema (PM-owned): account_id, ask_id, requested_points, delivery_window, required_engineering_domains, SLA_impact_flag, stakeholder_owner.
2) Implement reconciliation service (ENG-owned): lightweight microservice that consumes ledger entries and current cycle capacity snapshot from planning tool; returns risk_score and mitigation_suggestions.
3) Console UX: small dashboard tile and a reconciliation panel on the VIP intake flow. UX will allow PM/SE to accept mitigation or escalate to "Dedicated Runway" decision.
4) Rollout: pilot with 3 top accounts for one cycle, iterate based on engineering feedback, then enable org-wide.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Trade-off: stricter gating reduces flexibility for fast commercial moments (e.g., urgent regulatory asks) but improves predictability. We'll add an "override" path but require Exec approval and timeboxed runway credits.
- Open question: how to convert qualitative asks into requested_points consistently. Proposal: template in intake form for required user flows + PM estimate.
- Dependency on capacity snapshot accuracy: if engineering capacity data lags, risk score will be noisy. Plan: ensure planning tool snapshots are refreshed nightly for pilot.

Rollback/fallback:
If pilot shows false positives (too many "cannot commit" results), we will temporarily relax gating and add a human review layer. If the reconciliation service is misaligned, disable automated enforcement and surface manual advisories only.

Operational notes:
- Initial ledger and rules are low-friction JSON schema stored in Confluence and synced to a Dynamo table (ENG).
- Reconciliation job runs nightly and on-demand when intake submissions occur.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Asha Patel (owner), Liam O'Connor (lead PM for console integration)
- Eng: Ranita Singh (backend owner), Mark Liu (infra)
- Sales/CS: Priya Desai (VP CS)
- Legal/Compliance: TBD for regulated requests

Next steps (this ticket scope):
- Finalize PRD and ledger schema (PM) -> due 2026-01-20
- Backend spike for reconciliation algorithm -> ENG spike (2 days) -> due 2026-01-25
- Console tile mockups and UX review (Design) -> due 2026-02-01
- Pilot gating policy and exec override process -> due 2026-02-05

Notes on alignment with OKRs:
- This initiative maps to OKR: "Improve roadmap predictability for top accounts" and contributes to the Reliability & Revenue retention objective by reducing emergency work and SLA exposures.
